previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old man with a history of coronary artery disease, diabetes, hypertension, and prior pulmonary embolism on warfarin presented with pleuritic chest pain, cough, and shortness of breath. He was subtherapeutic on admission with an INR of 1.4. A CT angiogram showed minimal partially occlusive filling defects consistent with resolving pulmonary emboli and no acute clot. Cardiac enzymes were negative, and the pain was attributed to pleural irritation from healing clots. He was started on a heparin drip and transitioned to enoxaparin for bridging while adjusting warfarin. His chronic conditions remained stable, and he was discharged home with instructions to continue anticoagulation, monitor for worsening symptoms, and obtain an INR check in clinic.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ y/o ___ speaking man with history significant for CAD s/p 
multiple PCI's, DM2, HTN, PE/DVT (on coumadin) presenting to the 
ED with dyspnea on exertion. 

#Dyspnea on Exertion with Hypoxia 
The patient reported DOE with right sided CP. A desaturation 
event to the 80%'s was noted int the ED.  PE and MI were ruled 
out by negative CTA, unchanged EKG and negative troponins x 3.  
Other etiologies of the patient's dypnea include CHF 
exacerbation, but this is unlikely in the setting of low BNP and 
apparent euvolemia on exam. Repeat ECHO was stable from prior. 
CXR in the ED was initially read as concerning for pneumonia, 
however this was felt to represent possible atelectasis as seen 
on CTA and patient did not clinically appear to have pneumonia.  
Patient remained comfortable on room air and had an ambulatory 
sat of 95%.  Patient's ride sided chest discomfort was 
reproducible to palpation and he was started on Tylenol and 
ibuprofen for presumed costochondritis.    

#CAD s/p multiple PCIs: troponins were cycles x3 and negative, 
multiple EKGs were taken while patient complained of dyspnea and 
chest pressure without evidence of ischemia.  He was continued 
home ASA, Plavix, metoprolol.  

#Insulin-Dependent DM: held metformin in house, started ISS

#Hypertension: continued isosorbide, diltiazem and valsartan.  
Lasix initially held due to hypotensive epidsode in the ED but 
restarted upon discharge.
  
#Hyperlipidemia: continued home statin 
 
#DVT/PE on Warfarin: continued home warfarin regimen, INR 2.5 
prior to discharge.

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES
# has follow up with PCP, patient to have magnesium checked with 
results faxed to PCP as was noted to be low during this 
hospitalization
